rationale: The answer gets the central mechanism right. It says both classes share one portfolio, that ETF-class in-kind redemptions under §852(b)(6) remove low-basis securities without the fund recognizing gain, and that this can shrink capital gains distributions for all classes, including the mutual fund class. It also correctly says cash-based trading can still realize gains, that cash mutual fund redemptions can force gain-realizing sales, and that the benefit depends on redemption volume and which lots are delivered. However, several key-point elements are missing. (1) It never says the remaining securities keep their original basis, so this removes embedded gains rather than stepping up basis. (2) It does not say that mutual fund cash flows can impose gains and costs on ETF-class holders; it frames the problem only as a partial offset to the shared benefit. (3) It does not say the fund-level nonrecognition rule leaves the gains of redeeming investors and authorized participants taxable. (4) It does not clearly state that the benefit is not guaranteed and depends on fund strategy and practical in-kind capacity. Because the core mechanism is correct but substantive limits from the second and third key points are omitted, the grade is partial.
